tb-407-1.question:
A conducting ring is moving away from a long straight wire carrying a stable d.c. (Fig a).

What is the direction of the current induced in the ring?

A Clockwise

B Anticlockwise

C An a.c. is induced in the ring.

D There is no induced current.
tb-407-1.reasoning: The stable d.c. in the wire produces a magnetic field pointing into the page at the position of the ring. When the ring moves away from the wire, the magnetic flux through the ring decreases. A current in the clockwise direction is induced to oppose the change.

tb-407-2.question:
A bar magnet is being pulled away from a solenoid at constant velocity by force F as shown (Fig b).

Which of the following is/are correct?

(1) The solenoid is attracted by the magnet.

(2) An induced current flows from X to Y through the galvanometer.

(3) The pulling force F is balanced by the magnetic force acting on the magnet.

A (3) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-407-2.reasoning:
When the magnet is pulled away, by Lenz’s law, an N-pole is induced on the left side of the solenoid to oppose the motion of the magnet.

∴ (1) is correct.

By right-hand grip rule, the induced current flows from Y to X through the galvanometer.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

The magnet moves at a constant velocity. The net force acing on the magnet is zero.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-407-5.question:
(For Q5–6.) A metal rod XY of length L is moving in a uniform magnetic field B at a constant velocity v (Fig d). The magnetic field points into the page and the rod moves to the right. The rod is perpendicular to the magnetic field and makes an angle of 30° to v.

Which of the following statements is incorrect?

A A steady current is induced in the rod.

B There is no work done on the rod due to the magnetic field.

C End X becomes positively charged while end Y becomes negatively charged.

D The voltage across XY will increase if L increases.
tb-407-5.reasoning:
The rod is not part of a closed circuit. There is no current in the rod.

∴ A is incorrect.

There is no magnetic force acting on the rod since there is no induced current.

∴ B is correct.

By Fleming’s right-hand rule, X is at a higher potential than Y.

∴ C is correct.

The rod will sweep over a larger area in the same time period if L increases.

∴ D is correct.

tb-407-6.question:
(For Q5–6.) A metal rod XY of length L is moving in a uniform magnetic field B at a constant velocity v (Fig d). The magnetic field points into the page and the rod moves to the right. The rod is perpendicular to the magnetic field and makes an angle of 30° to v.

Find the potential difference across XY.

A 0

B BLv sin 30°

C BLv cos 30°

D BLv
tb-407-6.reasoning:
Area swept by the rod in Δt = vΔt (L sin30°)

E.m.f. induced =ΔΦΔt

=BvΔt(Lsin30°)Δt

= BLv sin 30°

tb-407-7.question:
A metal plate can rotate freely around an axle. The set-up is placed between two unlike magnetic poles (Fig e). The plate is given a sharp push and starts rotating.

What will happen to the metal plate afterwards?

(1) The plate will be slowed by the field.

(2) It will become hot.

(3) Eddy currents flow in the plate.

A (3) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-407-7.reasoning:
By Lenz’s law, eddy currents are induced to oppose the motion of the metal plate.

∴ (1) and (3) are correct.

The eddy current heats up the plate.

∴ (2) is correct.

tb-407-8.question:
Which of the following statements about a search coil is/are correct?

(1) It measures the component of magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the coil.

(2) A search coil with more turns is more sensitive.

(3) It can be used to measure a steady magnetic field.

A (1) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-407-8.reasoning:
Induced e.m.f. = NΔΦΔt= NΔ(BA)Δt

where B is the component of the magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the coil.

∴ (1) and (2) are correct.

A steady magnetic field does not induce an e.m.f. in a search coil.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-407-9.question:
A metal coil PQRS is put in a uniform magnetic field (Fig f).

Which of the following actions can induce a current flowing in the coil?

(1) Moving the coil towards the left within the magnetic field.

(2) Increasing the strength of the field.

(3) Rotating the coil about SP.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-407-9.reasoning:
Number of field lines through the coil is unchanged.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

Number of field lines through the coil increases.

∴ (2) is correct.

Number of field lines through the coil changes periodically.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-407-11.question:
(For Q11−12.) Figure h shows two parallel long straight wires carrying currents of the same size.

What is the direction of the induced current flowing in the loop?

Option

at time t1

at time t2

A

clockwise

clockwise

B

clockwise

anti-clockwise

C

anti-clockwise

clockwise

D

anti-clockwise

anti-clockwise
tb-407-11.reasoning:
The magnetic field at midway between the two parallel wires is zero.

When the loop is at position X is moving to the right, the field lines through it point into the page and the number of field lines is decreasing.
